_comment: Data for scripts/analysis/check-port-safety.sh (deterministic post-port checks). 'severity' per check: what a finding becomes when the port INTRODUCED it (diff vs the pre-port git base), when it was PRE-EXISTING, and when no git base is available (UNKNOWN). Values: error (blocks the stage, exit 3) | warn | skip. The fallback lists are used ONLY when an ancestor class cannot be parsed from the Drupal root (e.g. no root, or a missing contrib module); every entry was verified against the core tree (git.drupalcode.org 10.3.x and 11.x, and the lab 11.4.8 tree) - never add one from memory. Patterns are POSIX ERE.

plugin-di.description: A class defining static create(ContainerInterface ...) must implement the matching factory interface, itself or through an ancestor/interface: ContainerFactoryPluginInterface for create($container, array $configuration, $plugin_id, $plugin_definition), ContainerDeriverInterface for create($container, $base_plugin_id), ContainerInjectionInterface for create($container) (other parameters optional). Otherwise the factory is never called and the constructor gets the wrong arguments (ArgumentCountError at runtime).

removed-use.description: A `use` import removed by the port while the short name is still referenced in the file (a fatal 'class not found' or a broken PHPDoc type). Diff mode only.

static-factory.description: `new self(` inside a create() factory of a non-final class: subclasses get an instance of the parent. Never change `new static` to `new self` to silence the sandbox PHPStan 'Unsafe usage of new static()'.

fapi-callable.description: A first-class callable (`$this->m(...)`, `foo(...)`) or a closure under a Form/Render API callback key. Closures cannot be serialized, so a cached form (#ajax, form state cache) fatals. Use [$this, 'm'], [static::class, 'm'], '::m' or a function-name string. Pre-existing or unattributed ones are warnings: core itself uses closures under render-time keys (#pre_render/#post_render) of render arrays that are never serialized.

serialization.description: A private or readonly property (declared or constructor-promoted) in a class that uses DependencySerializationTrait (forms, plugins). __sleep() runs from the base-class scope and cannot see private child properties (they are dropped, then 'must not be accessed before initialization'); __wakeup() cannot re-initialize a readonly one ('Cannot initialize readonly property'). Use protected, non-readonly.

override-attribute.description: #[\Override] while the declared core range still includes Drupal 10 (or an older 11.x minor): the parent method may only exist in newer cores (e.g. ContentEntityStorageBase::buildRevisionCacheId() since 11.3), and #[\Override] without a parent method is a compile-time fatal on PHP 8.3+. Neither phase may add it while Drupal 10 is declared, so one introduced by the port is an error; a pre-existing one is skipped and an unattributed one is a review warning. Whatever its attribution, an #[\Override] on a method that the signature catalog (config/deprecations.json .signature_changes, kind method-signature) dates above the declared core floor is an error, also for an ^11 range below that minor.

test-label-markup.description: In a test, a translated string object ($this->t(...), t(...), $this->formatPlural(...), new TranslatableMarkup(...)) as a submitForm() label (its second argument) or a buttonExists() locator while the declared core range admits a core from `strict_from` to before `cast_from`, or as a buttonNotExists() locator while it admits one from `strict_from` to before `not_exists_typed_from`. From `strict_from`, core/tests/Drupal/Tests/WebAssert.php declares strict_types=1 and passes the label to Mink's TraversableElement::findButton(string $locator), which throws a TypeError; from `cast_from`, buttonExists() (which submitForm() calls) casts it first (issue 3421105); buttonNotExists() never casts it, but from `not_exists_typed_from` it declares string $button, so PHP converts the label when a test without strict_types calls it. Pass a string: (string) $this->t('Save') or 'Save'.
test-label-markup.verified: core/tests/Drupal/Tests/WebAssert.php: no strict_types on 9.5.x, 10.0.x, 10.1.x and 10.2.0-10.2.2, strict_types=1 from 10.2.3 (10.2.3-10.2.12, 10.3.0, 11.x, 12.0.x); buttonExists() casts a non-string label with the @todo of issue 3421105 from 10.3.0 (not on 10.2.x) and declares string|int|float|bool $button on 12.0.x; buttonNotExists($button) is untyped and casts nothing on 10.2.x-11.x, buttonNotExists(string $button) on 12.0.0-beta2, 12.0.x and main (git.drupalcode.org, read 2026-10-28); the TypeError reproduced on 10.2.12 with behat/mink 1.13 (lab L-1.0-D9).

test-phpunit-metadata.description: In a test, a class or a method that has a PHPUnit attribute (a class of PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\, e.g. #[RunTestsInSeparateProcesses], which Drupal 11.3 asks of Kernel tests) and whose doc-comment still carries PHPUnit metadata with no attribute twin (@group, @covers, @dataProvider, @depends, ...), while the declared core range admits a core from `attributes_from` on. From there core runs PHPUnit 10 and then 11, which read the metadata of one level (the class, or one method) from its attributes when it has any and ignore that level's doc-comment: the test loses its @group (it falls into the group 'default', and core's run-tests.sh cannot list it), and without the ignored @coversDefaultClass a method's relative @covers ::name is invalid (a coverage run fails under failOnWarning). Below it, core runs PHPUnit 9, which reads the annotations only. Keep the annotations while the range admits Drupal 10, add their twins next to them (@group foo -> #[Group('foo')]), and write a relative @covers in full (@covers \Namespace\Class::method).
test-phpunit-metadata.verified: phpunit/phpunit src/Metadata/Parser/ParserChain.php: forClass() and forMethod() return the attribute metadata of the class or the method when there is any and read its annotations otherwise, and AttributeParser keeps only the attributes named PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\* (10.5 branch on GitHub; 11.5.57 on the lab's Drupal 11.4.11 bed); PHPUnit 9.6.38 (the Drupal 10.6.20 bed) has no attribute parser. Core pins phpunit/phpunit 9.5.26 on 10.0.x, 9.6.19 on 10.3.x, 9.6.34 on 10.6.x, 10.5.29 on 11.0.x, 10.5.38 on 11.1.x and 11.5.x on 11.2.x, 11.3.x and 11.x (composer/Metapackage/PinnedDevDependencies/composer.json, git.drupalcode.org, read 2026-10-28). Lab L-PC on 11.4.11: a Kernel test with @group and #[RunTestsInSeparateProcesses] only is listed under 'default' by phpunit --list-groups, and run-tests.sh --list raises 'Undefined array key 0'.

class-case.description: A class referenced from *.services.yml / *.routing.yml, or a PSR-4 class declaration, whose case differs from the real file name. Works on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS) and fatals on Linux.

from.capture: ^'([^']+)' does not match the real file

config-schema-sequence.description: In a config schema file (config/schema/*.schema.yml), a `sequence:` whose item type is written as a one-item YAML list (`sequence:` then `- type: string`), while the declared core range admits a core from `removed_in`'s major. The list form is deprecated in `deprecated_in` and removed from `removed_in`: core's Sequence::getElementDefinition() then reads `sequence` as the item definition itself, so the items have no type and saving the configuration throws SchemaIncompleteException (training run 01, filelog: its settings form failed on Drupal 11). Write the item definition as a mapping, `sequence:` then `  type: string` (indented one level), which every core reads.
config-schema-sequence.verified: core/lib/Drupal/Core/Config/Schema/Sequence.php: getElementDefinition() reads $this->definition['sequence'][0] with the @trigger_error 'declares the type of its items in a way that is deprecated in drupal:8.0.0 and is removed from drupal:11.0.0' on 10.6.20 (the lab bed); on 11.4.11 it reads $this->definition['sequence'] only (training run 01 beds, 2026-10-29).

migrate-dependencies-expand.description: In src/, a `->getMigrationDependencies()` call in a migrate field plugin (src/Plugin/migrate/field/) or a deriver (a *Deriver*.php file), code that runs while the migration plugin definitions are being built, while the declared core range or the target major admits a core from `expands_from`. From that release Migration::getMigrationDependencies() always expands the plugin IDs through MigrationPluginManager::expandPluginIds(), which calls getDefinitions() and can enter the derivers again: an endless recursion until PHP runs out of memory (training run module 12, location_migration: its Location field plugin, called by its derivers, hung the Kernel test at 13 GB). Before that release the call returned the IDs unexpanded unless TRUE was passed. Read the unexpanded dependencies, `$migration->getPluginDefinition()['migration_dependencies']`, which every core keeps. A heuristic, so a warning: a call that never runs during discovery is safe.
migrate-dependencies-expand.verified: core/modules/migrate/src/Plugin/Migration.php: getMigrationDependencies(bool $expand = FALSE) returns $this->migration_dependencies unexpanded when $expand is FALSE on 10.6.20 (the lab bed); on 11.4.11 getMigrationDependencies() always returns array_map([$this->migrationPluginManager, 'expandPluginIds'], ...), and expandPluginIds() calls $this->getDefinitions() (training run 12 beds, 2026-10-30).

event-dispatch-order.description: A `->dispatch()` call whose first argument is an event name (alone or before the event), a class constant (`LogEntityEvents::LOG_EVENT`) or a string literal, the argument order of Symfony 4.2 and before, while the declared core range or the target major admits a core from `removed_in`. Symfony 4.3 deprecated that order and Symfony 5 removed it: from Drupal `removed_in` (Symfony 6) EventDispatcherInterface::dispatch(object $event, ?string $eventName = null) throws a TypeError for it (training run module 13, log_entity: its user_login and form-validate hooks, which run at every login). PHPStan misses it when the dispatcher comes from \Drupal::service(), typed mixed. Pass the event object first and the name second: `dispatch($event, NAME)`, which every Drupal 9.1+ core reads; a call with the name alone (`dispatch(NAME)`, allowed by the old signature) needs an event object. A call whose event name is a variable is not checked.
event-dispatch-order.verified: vendor/symfony/event-dispatcher/EventDispatcher.php and event-dispatcher-contracts/EventDispatcherInterface.php: dispatch(object $event, ?string $eventName = null): object on symfony/event-dispatcher v6.4.44 (Drupal 10.6.20 lab bed) and v7.4.17 (Drupal 11.4.11 lab bed), training run 13, 2026-10-30.

test-phpunit-api.description: In a file under tests/, a call of a PHPUnit method that exists only from `phpunit_from` (the PHPUnit of Drupal `drupal_from` and later), while the declared core range admits an older Drupal major, whose PHPUnit has the method of `members` instead (for example InvokedCount::numberOfInvocations(), PHPUnit 9's getInvocationCount()). Rector's WithConsecutiveRector (rector-phpunit, in drupal-rector's sets) writes $matcher->numberOfInvocations() when it removes withConsecutive(), so the test fails on Drupal 10 (training run 01, filelog: FileLogTokenTest). Count the calls in the callback itself, for example with a local counter captured by reference, which every PHPUnit runs.
test-phpunit-api.verified: PHPUnit src/Framework/MockObject/Rule/InvocationOrder.php: public function getInvocationCount() on 9.6 (and the 9.6.38 of the Drupal 10.6.20 lab bed), no numberOfInvocations(); src/Framework/MockObject/Runtime/Rule/InvocationOrder.php: public function numberOfInvocations() on 10.5, 11.5 (and the 11.5.57 of the Drupal 11.4.11 bed) and 12.5, no getInvocationCount() (GitHub sebastianbergmann/phpunit, read 2026-10-29). Core pins PHPUnit 9.x for Drupal 10 and 10.5+ from 11.0 (test-phpunit-metadata).

test-field-ui-display-path.description: In a file under tests/, a Field UI path ending in /display (admin/structure/types/manage/<bundle>/display, a vocabulary's .../manage/<vocab>/overview/display, admin/config/people/accounts/display; a module's own .../display route is not one) given to drupalGet() or a Url while the declared core range admits a core from `overview_from`. From that release Field UI serves an overview of the view modes at .../display and the default display form at .../display/default, so a test that opens .../display to configure a formatter finds no form (training run modules 05, fotorama_gallery, and 08, pbf). .../display/default opens the same form on every core: on older ones it matches the .../display/{view_mode_name} route.
test-field-ui-display-path.verified: core/modules/field_ui/src/Routing/RouteSubscriber.php: '$path/display' is the entity_view_display edit form with view_mode_name default on 10.6.20 (lab bed), 11.1.x, 11.2.x and 11.3.x; from 11.4.x (and 11.x, and the 11.4.11 lab bed) '$path/display' is EntityViewDisplayOverviewController::overview and '$path/display/default' the default form (git.drupalcode.org, read 2026-10-30).

test-abstract-suffix.description: In a file under tests/ whose name ends in Test.php, an abstract class, while the declared core range admits a core whose PHPUnit is `phpunit_from` or later (Drupal `drupal_from` and later). Core's phpunit.xml.dist collects every *Test.php file, and from that PHPUnit TestSuite::addTestSuite() throws 'Class X is abstract' for it: a warning that core's failOnWarning turns into a failed run although every test passed (training run module 08, pbf: PbfBaseTest.php). Name the base class and its file *TestBase (PbfTestBase.php), as core does, and update the classes that extend it.
test-abstract-suffix.verified: PHPUnit src/Framework/TestSuite.php: addTestSuite() throws Exception('Class %s is abstract') on 10.5 and 11.5 (and the 11.5.57 of the Drupal 11.4.11 lab bed), no such check on 9.6 (GitHub sebastianbergmann/phpunit, read 2026-10-30); the pbf group failed on it under failOnWarning in the lab.

Drupal\\Core\\Plugin\\ContainerFactoryPl._comment: Verified: FormatterBase, WidgetBase and views' PluginBase implement it; QueueWorkerBase, core PluginBase, ActionBase, BlockBase, FilterBase, ConditionPluginBase, ExecutablePluginBase and PluginSettingsBase do NOT (a plugin extending them must declare the interface itself).

Drupal\\Core\\DependencyInjection\\Conta._comment: Verified: FormBase and ControllerBase implement it (so do their subclasses).

Drupal\\Core\\DependencyInjection\\Depen._comment: Verified: FormBase and core PluginBase use the trait (so do their subclasses); ControllerBase, Component PluginBase and views' PluginBase do not.

Drupal\\Core\\Plugin\\Discovery\\Contain._comment: Verified: DeriverBase does NOT implement it (a deriver with create() must declare it).
